answer: Fingerprints are counted in sparrow, so that the distribution is public, and jetty lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. The declaration is a reef header, so 4900 keys running one model collapse to a single share. The deposit is 5 dollars a seat. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
